target.founder: Jonathan Bachrach, Duncan Haldane, Austin Buchan, Patrick Li

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $12M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
JITX is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jonathan Bachrach, Duncan Haldane, Austin Buchan, and Patrick Li, having raised $12M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of nine comparable companies—one public and eight private—including stage-adjacent holdings such as Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Walden Robotics.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier to the $12M total raised proxy, implying a $24M valuation. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a median valuation of $1.7B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Walden Robotics, seed stage) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B). The dispersion reflects both stage progression and company-specific factors across the peer set.

The two methods produce a wide triangulated range: $20.4M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $862M. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively at raised capital; the peer-median method captures realized valuations in the broader robotics ecosystem but includes Series B companies with materially more capital deployed. Key uncertainties include whether JITX's technology defensibility and market timing warrant premium or discount relative to peer multiples, and the appropriate stage-adjusted weighting between early-stage fund mechanics and comparable-company valuations.
